scanner_doubts: likelihood_var.md:351,357 - qe-math-006 is reported as 0 for this file, but both of these displays contain a top-level alignment tab inside a bare `$$` with no alignment environment: line 351 is `A_f & = \begin{bmatrix} 0.7 & 0.2 \\ 0.1 & 0.6 \end{bmatrix}, \quad C_f = ...` and 357 is the same shape for $A_g$ and $C_g$. A `$$` display compiles as `\[ ... \]`, where `&` is "Misplaced alignment tab character &" - the same class of PDF build failure that makes qe-math-006 a Critical rule, but with the environment missing altogether rather than being the wrong one, so the existing check (which looks for `align`/`align*` inside `$$`) does not see it. The detection has to be position-aware, because the `&` characters *inside* `\begin{bmatrix} ... \end{bmatrix}` on the same line are legitimate: flag an `&` that is not enclosed by any `\begin{...}...\end{...}` group within the display. These two lines are the only such sites in this lecture, and the pattern (an author writing an aligned pair of definitions and forgetting the environment) is common enough that it is worth a corpus-wide pass.
